# Set working directory
setwd("C:\\Users\\helin\\Desktop\\IIMT2641\\boston-house-price-modeling\\data\\")
# Install required packages
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cran.rstudio.com/"))
install.packages("tidyverse")
install.packages("factoextra")
# Load the libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(factoextra)
# Load the Boston dataset and check its structure
boston <- read.csv("boston_cleaned.csv")
str(boston)
# Standardize the data (exclude MEDV)
scaled_data <- scale(boston %>% select(-MEDV))
# Apply the Elbow Method to determine the optimal number of clusters
set.seed(123)
wss <- sapply(1:10, function(k) {
  kmeans(scaled_data, k, nstart = 25)$tot.withinss
})
# Plot the Elbow Method graph
plot(1:10, wss, type = "b", 
     xlab = "Number of clusters (k)", ylab = "Within-cluster sum of squares (WSS)",
     main = "Elbow Method")
# Perform K-means clustering with k=3
set.seed(123)
k <- 3  
km_result <- kmeans(scaled_data, centers = k, nstart = 25)
# Add cluster results to the dataset
boston$cluster <- km_result$cluster
# Perform PCA without centering and scaling
pca_result <- prcomp(scaled_data, center = FALSE, scale = FALSE)

# Prepare the data for PCA plot
pca_df <- data.frame(
  PC1 = pca_result$x[, 1],
  PC2 = pca_result$x[, 2],
  Cluster = as.factor(boston$cluster)
)

# Calculate explained variance for each principal component
var_explained <- pca_result$sdev^2 / sum(pca_result$sdev^2)
pc1_var <- round(var_explained[1] * 100, 1)
pc2_var <- round(var_explained[2] * 100, 1)

# Customized PCA plot
ggplot(pca_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = Cluster)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73")) +
  labs(
    x = paste0("PC1 (", pc1_var, "% Variance)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", pc2_var, "% Variance)"),
    title = "PCA of Housing Price Clusters",
    subtitle = "K-means clustering with k=3",  
    color = "Cluster Group"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  ) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 4)))
# View the median house prices by cluster
cat("Median house prices by cluster:\n")
aggregate(MEDV ~ cluster, data = boston, median)  # Now using median
# Create a boxplot to show the distribution of house prices by cluster
ggplot(boston, aes(x = factor(cluster), y = MEDV, fill = factor(cluster))) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Pastel1", name = "Cluster") +
  labs(
    x = "Cluster", 
    y = "Median House Price (MEDV)", 
    title = "House Price Distribution by Cluster (k=3)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
# Summarize the characteristics of each cluster
cluster_summary <- boston %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), mean))

# Display the summary result
print(cluster_summary)
